messages:
incident-bot: PagerDuty alert fired -> PD#INC-2026-4521. Alert: GPU memory pressure / CUDA OOM on inference-prod-eu-1. Affected pool: g-pool-0{3,5}. Severity: P1. Link: https://pagerduty.example/INC-4521

pagerduty: Alert details: service=redwood-runtime, check=GPU-Mem-Pressure, metric=gpu.mem.util>92% for 3m, error_samples=CUDA out of memory

Dave (oncall): acked on PagerDuty :hand: taking lead. Starting triage.

Alex (mlops): seeing repeated stack traces on g-pool-03: ```
2026-03-14T10:02:31Z ERROR inference-runtime: allocation failed: CUDA out of memory.
  at cuMemAlloc ...
  model=open_llama-13b-quant, seq_len=1024, batch=8, token_idx=512
```

Jess (sre): metrics: 503s up ~6% last 10m, p95 latency +180ms, error-rate spike correlates with GPU OOMs. Some customers seeing failed streams. Dashboard: https://grafana.redwood/boards/inf-prod

Ben (infra): copying node log from g-pool-05: ```
[kernel] GPU 0: ECC event, memory allocation failed, 0x7f3a...
[service] worker 42 crashed with SIGABRT after cudaMalloc failure
```

Maria (prod-eng): any recent rollout? did we push a model change or higher batch defaults?

Alex (mlops): No rollout in last 2 hours. We did increase default `runtime.batch_target_tokens` for some routes in canary earlier today (to improve throughput). Suspect batch sizing interacting with quant variant.

Dave (oncall): Immediate mitigations: 1) reduce batch target on live runtime to 1 for critical routes 2) enable fallback to lower-memory model variant 3) cordon/drain affected nodes 4) page infra-ops if noisy hardware.

Ben (infra): running commands now: 
```
redwoodctl runtime update --cluster inference-prod-eu-1 --route "*/generate" --set batch_target_tokens=1
redwoodctl cluster cordon g-pool-03
redwoodctl cluster drain g-pool-03 --timeout 300s
```

infra-ops: acked and on it. We'll check driver/kernel logs and GPU telemetry.

Maria (prod-eng): enabling model fallback to open_llama-13b-8bit-quant for routes with high concurrency. Patch applied: `config set route.fallback_model=open_llama-13b-8bit-quant` . This should reduce memory by ~40% but slightly higher latency.

Alex (mlops): confirm: batching change + fallback in place. Monitoring OOMs... initial look: OOM events dropping after batch change on g-pool-05 but still occasional on g-pool-03.

Dave (oncall): customers impacted? Jess?

Jess (sre): small subset of requests served by g-pool-03 saw failures — ticketed customers: internal list shows 3 paying customers with degraded experience: cust-a, cust-b, cust-c. CS notified via outage email draft (sending now).

pagerduty: Escalation: paging infra-ops@redwood and hw-team-oncall.

infra-ops: investigating hardware; initial telemetry shows thermal throttling on GPU 0 of g-pool-03 and memory fragmentation leading to failed allocations. We'll attempt a soft reboot of the GPU driver on that host. ETA 10m.

Ben (infra): soft-driver-restart command run on g-pool-03: `sudo systemctl restart nvidia-driver.service` — monitoring.

Alex (mlops): while infra does driver restart, I recommend we proactively shift traffic off g-pool-03 by adding node selector to runtime: `--node-avoid g-pool-03` and scale up g-pool-07 (cold spare) by +2 GPUs.

Ben (infra): scaling g-pool-07 +2 GPUs now. Cmd: `cluster autoscale --pool g-pool-07 --add 2`

infra-ops: driver restart completed on g-pool-03. GPU telemetry stabilized but we still see fragmentation warnings. Suggest full node reboot if OOMs reoccur.

Dave (oncall): note for handoff: if OOMs persist after scale and driver restart, plan is to reboot g-pool-03 overnight (low traffic window) and run `cuda-memtest` across GPUs. Also consider pinning guest VM allocations to reduce fragmentation.

Sasha (next-oncall): I'll take follow-up in 30m. Leaving a checklist: 1) confirm OOM rate stays <1/hr for 1h 2) confirm customer errors cleared 3) coordinate node reboot if needed 4) update incident ticket with timeline.

Maria (prod-eng): CS update posted. Customer-facing status page updated: short degradation, mitigation in progress.

Dave (oncall): creating incident doc INC-2026-4521 in incidents/ with timeline. Adding postmortem owner = alex.

Alex (mlops): quick note about long-term fix: evaluating changing default quantization layout and adding periodic defragmentation during low load. Filing follow-up RFC.

incident-bot: Incident INC-2026-4521 created: https://incidents.redwood/INC-2026-4521. Current status: mitigated (partial), monitoring.

Dave (oncall): handing off to Sasha. I'm leaving the thread; ping me if it spikes again. :thumbsup:

Sasha (next-oncall): ack. Taking over for monitoring and next steps. Will coordinate reboot if OOMs reappear.

infra-ops: final note: we saw GPU ECC warnings and memory fragmentation on g-pool-03; recommend RMA candidate if reboot + driver restart doesn't hold.

Dave (oncall): thanks everyone. Closing active paging for now — keep incident open for follow-up.
